text:
For two photons of energies \(E\) (high‑energy γ) and \(\varepsilon\) (CMB photon) colliding at an angle \(\theta\),

\[
s = 2E\varepsilon\,(1-\cos\theta)
\]

is the invariant mass squared of the system.  
Pair production requires

\[
\sqrt{s}\ge 2m_ec^{2}\;\;\Longrightarrow\;\; s\ge (2m_ec^{2})^{2}=4m_e^{2}c^{4}.
\]

For the most effective (head‑on) collision \(\theta=\pi\) so \(1-\cos\theta = 2\). Then

\[
2E\varepsilon\,(2)=4E\varepsilon \ge 4m_e^{2}c^{4}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
E\varepsilon \ge m_e^{2}c^{4}.
\]

Thus the threshold γ‑ray energy is

\[
E_{\text{thr}} = \frac{m_e^{2}c^{4}}{\varepsilon}.
\]

Insert the numbers  

\[
m_ec^{2}=0.511\;\text{MeV}=5.11\times10^{5}\,\text{eV},
\qquad
\varepsilon = 10^{-3}\,\text{eV},
\]

\[
m_e^{2}c^{4} = (5.11\times10^{5}\,\text{eV})^{2}
            \approx 2.61\times10^{11}\,\text{eV}^{2}.
\]

\[
E_{\text{thr}} = \frac{2.61\times10^{11}\,\text{eV}^{2}}{10^{-3}\,\text{eV}}
               = 2.61\times10^{14}\,\text{eV}
               = 2.6\times10^{5}\,\text{GeV}.
\]

Therefore the γ‑rays whose lifetimes are limited by annihilation on CMB photons have energies of order \(2.6\times10^{5}\) GeV.

**Answer: B**.
